partners.mechanism_chain: KCNJ11 (HGNC:6325) —DISRUPTS→ ATP-sensitive inwardly rectifying potassium channel activity (GO:0005404); ABCC8 (HGNC:26) —DISRUPTS→ ATP-sensitive inwardly rectifying potassium channel activity (GO:0005404); ATP-sensitive inwardly rectifying potassium channel activity (GO:0005404) —DECREASES→ insulin secretion (GO:0007221); insulin secretion (GO:0007221) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoglycemia (HP:0001284); insulin secretion (GO:0007221) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoglycemia, leucine-induced (HP:0000795). Loss-of-function mutations in KCNJ11 and ABCC8 disrupt the ATP-sensitive potassium channel (KATP channel) activity. For instance, diazoxide, a KATP channel opener, is used to treat hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia, highlighting the potential for targeting this channel. partners.mechanism_chain: Pathogenic variant in KCNJ11 (PMID:10970040) —DISRUPTS→ KCNJ11 (HGNC:6502); Pathogenic variant in ABCC8 (PMID:10970040) —DISRUPTS→ ABCC8 (HGNC:25474); KCNJ11 (HGNC:6502) —DISRUPTS→ ATP-sensitive potassium channel activity (GO:0005404); ABCC8 (HGNC:25474) —DISRUPTS→ ATP-sensitive potassium channel activity (GO:0005404); ATP-sensitive potassium channel activity (GO:0005404) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia (HP:0001991). Loss-of-function mutations in either KCNJ11 or ABCC8 disrupt the normal activity of the ATP-sensitive potassium channel (KATP channel), leading to its persistent open state. This persistent opening causes depolarization of the pancreatic beta-cell membrane, preventing calcium influx and thus inhibiting the closure of voltage-gated calcium channels. Consequently, insulin secretion remains inappropriately high, even in the fasting state, resulting in hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia.
